title: Neuropathy Phenotyping Protocols - Immunohistochemistry for Tissue Sections
author: Eva Feldman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7rfhm3n
materials: General Concepts: • Keep buffers consistent through fix, rinses, antibody dilutions and chromogen development. • Antibodies are sticky, always use plastic tips and tubes for storing, diluting and pipeting antibodies. • Check slides after each major step in the protocol to make sure sections are still stuck to the slide. There is no point in continuing if the sections have all been removed due to over zealous washes.
2º antibody labeled with red or green fluorochrome.

substeps.instruction: Remove slides from freezer and air dry on a warm plate.
Ring sections with a PAP pen.
If tissue was not fixed prior to embedding and sectioning, fix sections for 10-30 min at 4ºC using one of the following: 4% paraformaldehyde, 2% paraformaldehyde, or ice-cold 1:1 acetone:methanol.
Deparaffinize in Hemo-D.
Hydrate through a series of ethanol washes: 100%, 100%, 95%, 95%, 70%, 50%, and distilled water.
Ring sections with a PAP pen, ensuring sections do not dry.

steps.title: Pre-treat and Block Sections
steps.instruction: Prepare the tissue for antibody incubation using a humid chamber.

substeps.instruction: Hydrate in buffer for 5 min.
Rinse in 0.5% H2O2 in buffer (prepared as 5 ml 30% H2O2 in 300 ml buffer) for 10 min (skip this step for immunofluorescence and proceed to blocking).
Rinse 3 times for 10 min each in buffer.

Permeabilize and block for 10 minutes using 0.1% TX100 in buffer, 2% non-fat dry milk, and 1% serum (serum must be from the animal in which the secondary antibody is raised; e.g., if 1º is rabbit and 2º is goat anti-rabbit, use normal goat serum).

steps.title: Apply Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate sections with the primary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Dilute primary antibody in buffer containing 0.1% TX100 (refer to antibody book for specific dilutions).
Remove slides from blocking solution without rinsing; dab away excess fluid with filter paper.
Place 20-40 µl of primary antibody within the PAP pen ring.
Seal the incubation chamber by wrapping parafilm around the edge.
Incubate using one of the following conditions: overnight at 22ºC with parafilm, 36-48 hours at 4ºC with parafilm, or 2-4 hours at 37ºC (increase volume to 50-60 µl for 37ºC).
Rinse in buffer 3 times for 10 minutes each.
Turn off overhead fluorescent lights to decrease quenching.
Apply secondary antibody labeled with red or green fluorochrome.
Incubate for 1 hour at 22ºC.
Rinse 3 times for 10 min in buffer.
Counterstain with Bis-benzimide (1ug/ml in buffer) for 5 min.
Rinse in buffer.
Cover with Prolong (refer to Prolong SOP).
Apply secondary antibody labeled with biotin.
Incubate for 1 hour at 22ºC.
Rinse 3 times for 10 min in buffer.
Incubate in Avidin HRP for 1 hour at 22ºC (solution must be prepared 1 hour prior to use to equilibrate).
Rinse 3 times for 10 min in buffer.
Apply DAB.
Rinse 3 times for 10 min in buffer; collect the first rinse and add bleach to denature DAB (do not put bleach directly on the slides).
Dehydrate through graded ethanol: 50%, 70%, 95%, 95%, 100%, 100%, followed by 2 changes of Hemo-D.
Counterstain.
Mount coverslips to slides with Permount.
